items.topic: Where to store rule metadata content
items.context: Each rule needs ~5 markdown fields (detailed description, passing/failing examples, fix instructions, severity rationale). These are static for the current 5 rules. Options range from hardcoding in Go to external files.

options.label: Hardcode as struct literals in standards.go
options.rationale: Simplest approach. All rule definitions stay in one file. Easy to review and test. Only 5 rules, so maintenance burden is low. Recommended because it matches the existing pattern where rules are already hardcoded structs.

options.label: YAML/JSON config files loaded at startup
options.rationale: Separates content from code. Easier for non-developers to edit. But adds file I/O, parsing, and a new config dependency for what is currently a zero-config handler.

items.topic: Single-rule evaluation: query param vs new endpoint
items.context: Need to support evaluating one rule at a time. The existing endpoint is POST /api/v1/audit/evaluate/{scenario} which evaluates all rules. Two approaches: add a ?rule= query param, or create a new dedicated endpoint.

options.label: Add ?rule= query parameter to existing endpoint
options.rationale: Backward compatible — no param means all rules (existing behavior). Minimal code change: just filter the evaluators slice. ScannerPage continues working unchanged. Recommended for simplicity.

options.label: New endpoint POST /api/v1/audit/evaluate/{scenario}/rule/{ruleId}
options.rationale: More RESTful. Cleaner URL semantics. But adds a new route, duplicates evaluation logic or requires extraction, and the existing endpoint works fine with filtering.

items.topic: Markdown rendering approach in the UI
items.context: Rule metadata (examples, fix instructions) contains markdown with code blocks. The StandardsPage needs to render this. Need to determine if there's an existing markdown renderer in the brand-manager UI or if one needs to be added.

options.label: Use pre-formatted HTML/JSX instead of raw markdown
options.rationale: No dependency needed. Structure the content as JSX with <pre>/<code> blocks. Works for the simple content (code snippets + numbered lists). Recommended because it avoids a new dependency for what is primarily code examples and short instructions.

options.label: Add a lightweight markdown renderer (e.g. react-markdown)
options.rationale: Proper markdown rendering with full syntax support. Better if content gets more complex in the future. Adds a dependency.

options.label: Use dangerouslySetInnerHTML with a server-side markdown-to-HTML conversion
options.rationale: Keeps bundle small. But introduces XSS surface and server complexity.

items.freeform: Follow same approach (including custom components for things like code blocks) as other apps like git-control-tower

items.topic: Scenario name input UX for rule evaluation
items.context: Both per-rule and batch evaluation need a scenario name. The ScannerPage uses a simple text input. Options for the Standards page input pattern.

options.label: Shared scenario input at page top, reused for both per-rule and batch
options.rationale: User enters scenario name once at the top. Per-rule 'Check' buttons and 'Scan All' button all use that value. Avoids repeated input. Recommended for cleaner UX — most users will test one scenario at a time.

options.label: Independent input per rule card + separate batch input
options.rationale: Matches the spec's 'inline form' description literally. Allows checking different scenarios per rule. But creates input repetition and visual clutter.

items.text: The ScannerPage already calls evaluateScenario() and renders per-rule pass/fail results with colored dots. The audit result rendering pattern (green/red dots, rule_id, message) can be reused or adapted for the Standards page per-rule results, avoiding duplication.
